Came into this movie knowing it was classic, but it just doesn't feel like it hold up to modern standards. The visuals are outstanding, with wide shots of western scenery, big sets with tons of extras. The music is also iconic, even though I'd never seen this movie before the score is immediately recognizable. I can't really say anything good about the movie beyond that. The plot was boring, really nothing interesting about it. The acting wasn't great, or I just hated the characters. Maybe both. I kept thinking to myself that this felt like a bad Bollywood movie. High budget, over the top, unnecessarily long, poorly directed, and a bit cheesy. The audio even felt like it was a bad dub. At one point I had to check my video player's settings to make sure I was using the original audio it was so bad. For a movie to be centered around three characters, you really don't get to know them. They remain the same from the beginning to the end of the movie. Random plot points expound on the backgrounds of the character occasionally, but it's never meaningful. *Minor spoilers* When the Good and the Ugly are captured by Union soldiers, all of a sudden the Bad is a captain in the Union army. I kept thinking he had to have assumed someone's identity somehow or they would explain it further, but no. The man who is introduced in the beginning of the movie as an assassin who always kills his target once he's paid has somehow been a captain in the Union army this whole time. I usually like westerns, so to come out of this one so disappointed surprised me. This was a really hard movie to rate, because what it does well it does really well. What it doesn't do well, it really doesn't do well. It kind of reminds me of a lot of modern country music in a way, almost pandering to the audience without any substance. Overall, it falls short of being a good movie to me.

Three-way duel was awesome. Super interesting how after we are introduced to their "names" as shown in the freeze-frame, the next three hours are spent refusing to let the card match the man. The "good" is the first and only to shoot in the duel. The "bad" is no monster, just painted differently because of his background. And the "ugly" is the only one we got to know. These three words are not descriptions of men, but instead three traits that exist inside every man.

The Good, the Bad and the Ugly The Good, the Bad and the Ugly (1966) وسط فوضى الحرب الأهلية الأمريكية، يتنافس ثلاثة رجال شديدو الاختلاف الطيب الشرير، والقبيح في رحلة محفوفة بالخيانة والمواجهات للوصول إلى كنز مدفون. ومع تغير التحالفات باستمرار، يصبح من الصعب معرفة من يمكن الوثوق به تحفة من الويسترن السباغيتي تجمع بين الشخصيات الأيقونية، المبارزات الملحمية، الموسيقى الخالدة، والتوتر الذي يتصاعد حتى واحدة من أشهر النهايات في تاريخ السينما.

J'ai longtemps attendu avant de voir l'un des plus grand western qui existe. J'ai énormément doutais et mes craintes se sont avérées. Le film est long pour ce qu'il a, à raconter. Ce qui en soit n'est pas grave, mais quand, on s'attache si peu aux personnages cela devient trop vite ennuyant. À la poursuite d'un gros magot, on ne sait jamais vraiment pourquoi ils veulent tout cette argent (puisque tout ce qu'ils peuvent acheter, ils le volent). Je trouve que, les scènes d'action ont très mal vielli. À la fin, on ressent bien qu'ils ont vécu une longue aventure mais je n'ai rien ressenti de très grandiose ou jolie (contrairerement à "Lawrence d'arabie"). Malgré quelques coup d'éclat et qualités inhérentes aux western (tension, punchline, décor, musique), je n'ai éprouvé qu'ennui, à attendre la scène suivante jusqu'à l'interminable fin.

I'm beginning to feel that I'm more a fan of the revisionist and neo-westerns, that take the genre and stretch and shake out what it is and what it can be. This was a great disappointment after the brisk and entertaining Fistful of Dollars and absolutely did not need to be three hours long. Every moment when Tuco is on-screen is a crime against me. It feels like Leone engaged in his own self-parody, with a now much dumber Blondie and Tuco falling from shenanigan to shenanigan, they learn nothing and proceed to the next. I've read enough articles to see people analysing this film through the lens of the futility of war or the violence and cruelty of the Old West, but frankly, it offers such a simplistic and mean-spirited point of view that I just didn't enjoy its wanton brutality. There are some fantastic segments and cinematography in this (the climax, the bridge fight, the introduction of Angel Eyes, the walk through the desert and the church) but its interspersed by plodding, frustrating sections. It could've been great with a good edit, alas, it's clear Clint did this one for the money.

Little did I know that the extended edition is OVER 3 HOURS LONNGGGG. I was reallllly debating just getting up and leaving like half way through. But I persevered. And hated it.
